transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because the district added this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on top of my regular teaching load. I’m still getting through the days, but I feel wound up and discouraged, which isn’t really like me. And I’ve started putting off lesson plans and emails that I normally would just handle right away.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
About five months now—since they assigned me the rollout role in the middle of the school year.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy doing?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I still enjoy the things I usually do.
Does your worrying mostly center around this work situation, or does it spread to many different areas of your life?
Mostly this work situation. Ever since they added the bilingual rollout on top of my regular teaching, that’s what has me feeling wound up and discouraged.
Aside from feeling discouraged, have you been experiencing persistent sadness, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness?
I’m not sure I’d call it persistent sadness or hopelessness. I’ve mostly just felt discouraged about the situation at work.
Would you describe your mood over these past few months as feeling down or depressed?

I wouldn’t say depressed exactly. I’ve been more wound up and discouraged since they added that bilingual rollout to my regular teaching. It’s not really like me, and I’ve started putting off lesson plans and emails I normally would just handle.
